sermon.title: Slavery Explained
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In “Slavery Explained,” Pastor David G. Kincer links the curses in Deuteronomy 28 and Israel’s captivities to the “divine nature” promised in 2 Peter 1:4. He teaches a three-part path to freedom from the slavery of sin and Satan: admit you are wrong, seek Jesus, and repent, including the role of water baptism and the preached word.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor note: he says “Leviticus 20:33” where the verse he reads is Leviticus 26:33, and “1 John 8:34” where the verse is John 8:34. He dates the Assyrian captivity “about 720 AD, or BC,” and gives “604 or 605” for the Babylonian captivity as he said them. The captions garble a few names and words in the song about Paul (“Ananias,” “Demas” and others are not guessed) and the phrase “not so [unclear] on that” about schools in Africa and South America, shown as [unclear]. He makes strong statements about Islam and the Quran, communism, humanism, public schools, Pentecostal groups, the Jews and others; these are his own views.

chunks.section_question: What curses does Deuteronomy 28 list, and what kinds of “slavery” does he warn about today?
chunks.short_answer: He reads Deuteronomy 28:15 and says the curses include “famines,” “plagues,” “war” and “slavery.” He says people can be enslaved by communism, Islam and “humanism … by capturing your mind,” and that this is why “Christian schools are so important.”

All right: curses, misfortunes, calamities, things that are not pleasing to go through. And then he lists them. Famines: we call it an economical turndown. Plagues: that’s not just your common cold, that’s your bubonic plague, that’s your Asian influenza that kills just hundreds of thousands, millions of people. AIDS today is killing millions of people. It was just beautiful, and China’s being blessed with that movement, and we need that spread throughout the world and in America.

chunks.section_question: How does he say Israel went into captivity, and what does that show?
chunks.short_answer: He says Israel was enslaved several times in Judges “in their own homeland,” then taken by Assyria and Babylon, and later oppressed by Greece and Rome, with the temple destroyed in 70 AD. He says all of this happened “just like God said he would do,” and that God “doesn’t live in temples made with hands.”
chunks.text:
So we find, as you know by reading the Bible, that these things were accomplished in Judges. Israel went into captivity several times, from seven years to forty years, in their own homeland. In their own homeland they went into captivity to Mesopotamia, Moab, Canaan, Midian and the Philistines, but they stayed in their homeland. It’s just God brought another nation to enslave them in their own homeland. But his promise was, his correction was, “I’m going to take you out of your homeland.” All right. And so we find that the Assyrian Empire, in about 720 AD, or BC, came and took Israel into captivity. Two captivities, all right. It actually happened. They took them out, and there’s no Bible that these ever came back, unless they came back in the captivity of Babylon. But then in about 604 or 605 we have the Babylonian captivity, you see, coming, taking the Jews and the remaining people there into Babylonian captivity.

Now, Rome and Greece both enslaved the Jews while they were still in their own nation, all right, for four hundred years before Christ came. These nations came and enslaved the Jews in their own nation again, just like Judges. But in 70 AD the Roman army came, destroyed the temple in Jerusalem like Jesus said it would be. And I don’t know why they want to build it again, that’s nonsense. It’s totally against the Bible. But these end-time people have this temple being built again, and that’s foolish. God doesn’t live in temples made with hands. He is building a church, a spiritual house. Amen. That’s the building that we’re building today. But anyway, they took hundreds of thousands of Jews captive and made them slaves, all right, just like God said he would do. And the Jews still didn’t get it, many of them.

Now, a lot of Jews came to Christ, you know. In fact, the first people that came to Christ were Jews. All right. And so in that, second, before the Second World War, Germany enslaved the Jews, killed six million of them, enslaved the rest, forcing them into slave labor, all because they were Jews, just like God said he would do. Are you there?

chunks.text:

Ah, I love these clouds forming a heart here, to remind you. 2 Peter 1:3-4: “As Jesus’ divine power has given us all things... whereby are given unto us exceedingly great and precious promises.” Why did he give us these great promises? He answers the question: that through these you may be a partaker of the divine nature, a participator of the divine nature. Wow. When I got saved, everybody was so focused on the second coming they never even thought about the divine nature. They thought Jesus was coming any minute, coming in 1960, coming in 1972, coming, coming, coming, coming, come, come, come, come, come, and he hadn’t come yet. And, say, we were so looking and so focused on who had the right chart for the second coming that we lost sight of the divine nature.

We forgot all about that Jesus was born of a virgin, and he came into the world for a purpose, not only to die on the cross but to give us his divine nature. Hallelujah. We got so focused on prosperity. There are so many groups that teach that prosperity is Christianity, it’s righteousness, and the Bible plainly says that’s wrong. Now, he wants to bless you, but remember, heathens are rich. But we focus on prosperity, and they do it today especially on TV and radio. It’s embarrassing. They focus on purpose, positive thinking, purpose-driven, positive thinking. Prophecy, especially in Pentecostal groups, they so focus on prophecy, giving everybody a private prophecy. It’s horrible, and I can talk about us tongue talkers because I am one. And when you make mistakes, you got to clear it up. Could that be an amen?

chunks.section_question: What distractions does he say keep us from the divine nature: helping the poor, miracles and gifts?
chunks.short_answer: He says the American church brags about “helping the poor,” but “we need to help the poor in spirit.” He says Jesus “only healed one person” at the pool of Bethesda, that he was healed of valley fever, and that filling out a spiritual-gifts “form” is not in the Bible: “a gift is an ability.”
chunks.text:
And so we got all these distractions. Helping the poor is so big in the American church that they really think they’re great Christians because they help the addict and the poor and the homeless and all that the American government is giving money to and enabling them to be poor, and the church just gloats over and brags about how they’re helping the poor. And we need to help the poor in spirit. Are you there? “Blessed are the poor in spirit.” Why are they poor? They don’t know Jesus, they don’t know wisdom, they don’t have knowledge. That’s the riches they need. See, we’re distracted, and so we don’t see this nature of God. You don’t even hear it preached on hardly anywhere, that we can be partakers, and his purpose to come was for us to be partakers of his divine nature.

Phenomena again in the Pentecostal Spirit-filled areas, man, they’re all into miracles. A miracle a day keeps unbelief away, or something like that, and if you don’t have a miracle every day, there’s something wrong. Well, how many of you know Jesus went to the pool of Bethesda and only healed one person? Walked right over all of them and healed one person, ain’t that right? He didn’t heal them all. And we love the healings. God healed me of, uh, valley fever. They told me I was going to die in thirty, sixty days, and God healed me, and it’s great. My wife loved me staying alive. She didn’t want me dying, she had kids to raise. And the doctor said, “You have a miracle.” The doctor right there in his office said it twice: “You got a miracle, man, you should be dead.”

Are you there? But he, you know, it’s like he does it every day, but it’s nice when it happens. Amen. There’s nothing like that in the Bible. “Let me fill out this form and see what gift I got.” If you got a gift, you got a gift. A gift is an ability. If you got an ability, you can use it. If you don’t have it, you can’t use it. I don’t care what kind of form you fill out. And we’re so focused on gifts that we miss the promise of the divine nature.

chunks.section_question: What is the “second promise” given to Israel in slavery, and what must we admit? (Leviticus 26)

chunks.text:
Hallelujah. So we’re going to get into the second promise. We hit the first promise last week, the second promise this week. The second promise is directed to the Israelites when they were in slavery. Okay, the second pro-, it’s important that you know this: the second promise to bring them to the divine nature is directed to Israel when they were in slavery. Leviticus 20:33: “I will scatter you among the nations.” You’re going to be in slavery to other nations. Verse 40: “If” (what’s that magic word?), “if,” don’t forget that, you have a responsibility. If you do something, God will do something. When you do something, God will do something. “If they confess, they admit their iniquities and the iniquities of their fathers, that they have walked contrary to me and I have walked contrary to them.”

If you admit you were wrong, that’s the first thing. We got to admit we’re wrong. Americans have a really hard time admitting they’re wrong. I know over in China you guys don’t have that, you guys are special, but in America, us Americans have a hard time admitting we’re wrong, and that’s the first thing you got to do. You got to admit you’re wrong. Wrong according to the Bible, not your friend’s opinion, not your opinion. You’re wrong because you’re violating what God said is right. He says if you admit you’re wrong, if you confess your iniquities and the iniquities of your fathers. It’s important that you recognize the generation before you was wrong too, and Daniel brings that out very clearly. “And I have brought them unto the land of their enemies.” Say, God is involved in this.

“If” (what’s that magic word?), if you do something, God said, I will do something. “If then their uncircumcised hearts be humbled, and they then accept the punishment of their iniquity.” And Americans just can’t get it that economic turndowns come because God’s trying to get their attention. Plagues come because God’s trying to get their attention. America just don’t get it. They won’t admit it. They won’t admit that they’re having mental depression and anguish because they’ve turned from God. But if they will admit it, “if their uncircumcised hearts be humbled and they accept the punishment of their iniquity, then will I remember my covenant.” Ooh! Then he will remember. You see, see, it’s not my baptism certificate, it’s not my being filled with the Holy Ghost, it’s not my sinner’s prayer when I first got saved. It’s if I will admit I’m wrong today, God will remember his covenant, and his covenant is great.

Are you there? Hallelujah.

chunks.section_question: How do we seek the Lord, and what is the difference between a song service and a worship service? (Deuteronomy 4:27-29)
chunks.short_answer: He says seeking God means “prayer,” “fasting,” “praise and worship” and “going to church,” and that “you should be coming to church for Jesus, not for social interaction.” He says there is “no mega church that can solve your problem. Only Jesus can,” and that in worship “we take on his nature.”
chunks.text:

chunks.text:

chunks.section_question: How does he say water baptism frees us from the slavery of sin? (Romans 6)
chunks.short_answer: He says baptism is not “an outward sign of an inward work,” because “he does something in water baptism.” Reading Romans 6:3-6 and 6:18, he says “I went down into the grave with Christ,” came out “in resurrection of life,” and became “a slave of righteousness,” and that it “pays to get baptized quick.”
chunks.text:
Water baptism is not an outward sign of an inward work. Man phrased that statement; it is not in the Bible. Prayer is not an outward sign of an inward work. Worship is not an outward sign of an inward work. There is a work going on. God honors his principles, and he gets involved and does things, and he does something in water baptism. Romans 6:3: “As many of us as were baptized into Jesus Christ were baptized into his” what? “Death.” Okay, “knowing this, that we were baptized into his death, that our old man was crucified with him, our old man of sin, that the body of sin might be done away with.” Wow. chunks.section_question: What does he say the divine nature is: no sin, and laying down his life? (1 John 3:5; John 10:17-18)
chunks.short_answer: He says the nature of God is like a seed or yeast that “gets in us and grows,” and that in Jesus “there is … no sin.” He says Jesus “chose to die in that fleshly body and rise again,” that “none of them could kill Jesus,” and that we partake of this nature.
chunks.text:
Hallelujah. Now, let’s look at the divine nature. If I’m to be a partaker of the divine nature, in closing here, what is the divine nature? And I wouldn’t dare to ask you to raise your hand and tell me, because most of us haven’t even thought about it. I know I didn’t for years. It had to take God to come and hit me over the head with a spiritual two-by-four to wake me up to things. The nature, the word nature, is growth by germination or expansion. You see, a seed germinates and it begins to expand and grow. You see, uh, yeast, as Jesus gave the parable of: you put a little yeast in a dough and it what? Spreads and infects the whole dough. So the nature of God, God’s divine nature, is that divine character of God that gets in us and grows.

See, when you’re first saved, you’re just a babe in Christ, you don’t know your head from your toe, but that thing in you begins to grow. Divine nature number one, 1 John 3:5: “You know that he was manifest to take away our sin.” You see, Jesus came, born of a virgin, in this Christmas season that we celebrate all over the world. Everywhere I go they celebrate Christmas, and they like their Christmas trees, and they don’t even have pine trees where I go, they get some kind of tree. And so this Christmas season is important to us. Our forefathers gave us this holiday, gave us Easter, and gave us Thanksgiving, and we need to protect the freedom of keeping these holidays. Could that be an amen? See, they want to take it away from us. Why?

Because these holidays point to an important thing in God, and the atheists and humanists don’t like it, so they fight against it. He came to take away our sins, and in him there is what? So what’s his divine character? No sin. And I am to be a partaker of the divine nature: no sin, not sinning. How many, we know we all sinners. Okay, so let’s watch how this works. Divine nature number two, John 10:17: “I laid down my life,” Jesus said. I die. I choose to die “that I might live again, that I might take my life up again. No man takes my life from me.” Satan can’t do it, the Roman Empire can’t do it, the Sanhedrin of the Jewish temple could not do it. No one could destroy Jesus. He laid down his life.

And this is where the Muslims are wrong. They say God cannot die. God can do anything. He chose to die in that fleshly body and rise again. So when we say the Jews killed Jesus, that’s not total truth. We say the Roman Empire killed Jesus, that’s not total truth. None of them could kill Jesus. He laid down his life, and he picked it back up again. How many know that’s power? Amen. And we get to partake of this divine nature. That is the divine nature. Let me show you: “I have power to take it, and I have power to lay it down. This commandment I received of my Father.” See, this is the law that God gave to Jesus: “I give you power to lay down your life for the sins of the world and pick up your life again, rise from the dead and ascend into the heaven.

chunks.section_question: Can Satan make us sin, and how do we live free from the slavery of sin? (1 John 2:1)
chunks.short_answer: He says “no man can make us sin,” and “Satan cannot make me sin. He can accuse me, he can tempt me, but he cannot make me sin.” He says we “choose to die through sin” and can “come alive again by confessing, seeking and repenting,” and that this is “the Christian’s divine nature.”
chunks.text:
I give you this power. That’s my commandment to you.” Well, if that’s God’s commandment to him, and we’re partakers of the divine nature, what is God’s commandment to us who believe on him? That sound fair? We have the same natural power, only we choose to die through sin. See, no man can make us sin. We choose to die through sin, and we can choose to come alive again by confessing, seeking and repenting from our sins, and we can live. Watch how this works: sin kills the spirit, [unclear] makes alive. Here’s the commandment we received of our Father. Unlike Jesus, who had no sin (I’m sure you all agree with that), we messed up, didn’t we? In fact, you probably messed up yesterday. You might have messed up this morning with a bad attitude, saying things you shouldn’t have said.

We are, we are good at this thing. Jesus had no sin. Unlike Jesus who had no sin, we become slaves of sin, Satan and spiritual death. But like Jesus, we have power to die by choosing to sin. “You are dead in trespasses and sin. Arise, you that sleepeth, arise from the dead, and Christ will give you life.” Arise from that sin. We also have power to live by choosing to be slaves of Jesus and righteousness. You see, I have the ability to go out here and sin today if I want to. I can go out and sin. I can choose that road, and I did as a young man. I didn’t follow God. I sinned really bad stuff. It doesn’t matter whether you’re a deep sinner or whether you’re a lightweight sinner, the punishment’s all the same, you know.

So if you’re going to be a sinner, it might as well just be a heavyweight sinner. You know, you’re going to burn in hell forever, it might as well be a heavyweight sinner. But I chose that. But when I was twenty years old, I chose Christ. I chose to admit I was wrong, I chose to seek Christ, I chose to return, turn from my sin, renounce sin and live for him, and Christ came to me and gave me life.

So our divine nature is to live free from the slavery of sin, the slavery of Satan and spiritual death, by Jesus’s death, by his resurrection, and obeying his word. Satan cannot make me sin. He can accuse me, he can tempt me, but he cannot make me sin. The sinners of this world can’t make me sin. It’s a choice I make. But if I confess my sin, and I seek Jesus, and repent, our divine nature is to do this anytime we find ourself a slave of sin. See, that is the Christian’s divine nature. If we do mess up, and 1 John 1 says, chapter 2, 1 John 2:1: “Beloved, I would that you not sin, but if you do sin, you have an advocate with the Father, even Jesus Christ the righteous.” See, I can go and I can be free from that slavery of sin by admitting I’m wrong, seeking Jesus, and repenting, and that’s the Christian nature.

That’s what makes us different from the world. Yeah, we make mistakes, we do things we shouldn’t do, but the nature God’s given us through his commandment is: I admit I’m wrong, I seek Jesus for the cleansing, the forgiveness and the deliverance from sin, and I turn from that sin. That’s the nature of the Christian. So the Christian keeps growing upward. Amen. Are you there? See, we keep taking on the nature of God. God had no sin, we do, but we keep gaining ground, because the nature he’s put within us is to admit we’re wrong, seek Jesus, and repent from that wrong.

faqs.question: What curses does he list from Deuteronomy 28?
faqs.answer: He lists “famines,” “plagues,” “war” and “slavery,” and says they come when “you violate God’s word.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: “But it shall come to pass, if you do not obey the voice of the LORD your God, to observe carefully all His commandments and His statutes which I command you today, that all these curses will come upon you and overtake you:

faqs.question: What does he say about communism, Islam and humanism?
faqs.answer: He says communism and Islam “want to enslave the world,” and that “humanism is out to enslave the world by capturing your mind.” He says that is why he wants kids out of public schools “where they’re indoctrinated with humanism, atheism.”

faqs.question: What does he say the church focused on instead of the divine nature?
faqs.answer: He says prosperity, “positive thinking,” “prophecy” and miracles: “we got so focused on prosperity,” and he adds that “heathens are rich.”

faqs.question: What does he say about prophecies that do not come true?
faqs.answer: He says “when a prophet doesn’t come to pass, they are what? False prophets,” and “when you say something’s going to happen and it doesn’t, then you’re a false prophet.”

faqs.question: Does he say Jesus healed everyone?
faqs.answer: No. He says Jesus “only healed one person” at the pool of Bethesda and “didn’t heal them all,” though “it’s nice when it happens.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Now there is in Jerusalem by the Sheep Gate a pool, which is called in Hebrew, Bethesda, having five porches. In these lay a great multitude of sick people, blind, lame, paralyzed, waiting for the moving of the water. For an angel went down at a certain time into the pool and stirred up the water; then whoever stepped in first, after the stirring of the water, was made well of whatever disease he had. Now a certain man was there who had an infirmity thirty-eight years. When Jesus saw him lying there, and knew that he already had been in that condition a long time, He said to him, “Do you want to be made well?” The sick man answered Him, “Sir, I have no man to put me into the pool when the water is stirred up; but while I am coming, another steps down before me.” Jesus said to him, “Rise, take up your bed and walk.” And immediately the man was made well, took up his bed, and walked. And that day was the Sabbath.

faqs.question: What does he say is the first thing we must do?
faqs.answer: He says “you got to admit you’re wrong,” and that it is “wrong according to the Bible, not your friend’s opinion, not your opinion.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: ‘But if they confess their iniquity and the iniquity of their fathers, with their unfaithfulness in which they were unfaithful to Me, and that they also have walked contrary to Me, and that I also have walked contrary to them and have brought them into the land of their enemies; if their uncircumcised hearts are humbled, and they accept their guilt— then I will remember My covenant with Jacob, and My covenant with Isaac and My covenant with Abraham I will remember; I will remember the land.

faqs.question: What does he say about prayer and mega churches?
faqs.answer: He says people say “a little two-minute prayer” but “don’t get down on their knees and seek God,” and that “there’s no mega church that can solve your problem. Only Jesus can.”

faqs.question: What is the difference between a song service and a worship service?
faqs.answer: He says “in a worship service, in a praise service, you touch Jesus. In a song service, you touch the song. It’s all about the music.”

faqs.question: Why does he say we take on the nature of what we spend time with?
faqs.answer: He says “you can’t have a meeting with God without taking on his nature,” and “what you spend time with, you become like. So when I spend time with Jesus, I become like Jesus.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: But the hour is coming, and now is, when the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth; for the Father is seeking such to worship Him.

faqs.question: Does he say baptism is only an outward sign?
faqs.answer: No. He says “water baptism is not an outward sign of an inward work. Man phrased that statement; it is not in the Bible,” and that “he does something in water baptism.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Or do you not know that as many of us as were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into His death? Therefore we were buried with Him through baptism into death, that just as Christ was raised from the dead by the glory of the Father, even so we also should walk in newness of life. For if we have been united together in the likeness of His death, certainly we also shall be in the likeness of His resurrection, knowing this, that our old man was crucified with Him, that the body of sin might be done away with, that we should no longer be slaves of sin.

faqs.question: What does he say Satan is?
faqs.answer: He says Satan “is a spirit” and “doesn’t have horns and a long tail and all that garbage,” and that “God created Satan.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: And you He made alive, who were dead in trespasses and sins, in which you once walked according to the course of this world, according to the prince of the power of the air, the spirit who now works in the sons of disobedience, among whom also we all once conducted ourselves in the lusts of our flesh, fulfilling the desires of the flesh and of the mind, and were by nature children of wrath, just as the others.

faqs.question: Who does he say can save you?
faqs.answer: He says “Jesus can only save you. Jesus can only forgive you. Jesus can only cleanse you of sin,” and that “your church can’t get you saved.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Now is the judgment of this world; now the ruler of this world will be cast out. And I, if I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all peoples to Myself.”

faqs.question: Does he say the Jews or the Romans killed Jesus?
faqs.answer: He says “none of them could kill Jesus. He laid down his life, and he picked it back up again,” so saying either group killed Jesus is “not total truth.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: “Therefore My Father loves Me, because I lay down My life that I may take it again. No one takes it from Me, but I lay it down of Myself. I have power to lay it down, and I have power to take it again. This command I have received from My Father.”

faqs.question: Does he say sinning is a choice?
faqs.answer: Yes. He says “we have power to die by choosing to sin,” and “we also have power to live by choosing to be slaves of Jesus and righteousness.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Therefore He says: “Awake, you who sleep, Arise from the dead, And Christ will give you light.”

faqs.question: What does he say a Christian does when they mess up?
faqs.answer: He says “I admit I’m wrong, I seek Jesus for the cleansing, the forgiveness and the deliverance from sin, and I turn from that sin,” and “that’s what makes us different from the world.”
